findings.finding: Agents could see a configuration request hash only after review and could not bind candidate/context bytes before execution.
findings.repair: Added `driftproof fingerprint` and `fingerprint_for_agent`, separating configuration identity from a candidate/context/tool-version content fingerprint.
validation: control destinations/run IDs do not change fingerprint
fingerprint configuration hash equals every concurrent navigation request hash

findings.finding: Python agents had to start and validate the machine CLI protocol themselves.
findings.repair: Added typed `ReviewRequest`, `fingerprint_for_agent`, and `review_for_agent` APIs that use an argv subprocess, validate the strict response union, and enforce process/response exit agreement.

findings.finding: Independent callers that omitted both output and run ID could target the same default control path.
findings.repair: SDK assigns a process-unique control run ID only when callers provide neither output nor run ID; semantic request identity still excludes the control ID.

findings.finding: A wrapper could accidentally accept malformed stdout or a response whose exit code disagreed with the process.
findings.repair: SDK validates exactly one `DriftProofAgentProtocolResponse`, redacts bounded stderr on parse failure, and rejects exit disagreement.
validation: unknown partial state never returned as success

findings.finding: New agent helpers could have worked only from the source checkout if omitted from the wheel.
findings.repair: Qualified fingerprint and SDK imports from a freshly installed wheel and exercised the installed one-object error path.
